chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Gigging in Los Angeles in 1947 and Nat Cole's turn to singing
summary: Simmons gigged with Happy Johnson and others; Nat Cole refused marijuana to protect his voice and made new records.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Yeah, I was playing professionally. I was gigging, gigging, gigging. Whoever had a gig.

Oh, I worked with Happy Johnson's Big Band for a while. Different ones off a -- Central Avenue would come up with a gig occassionally. Like the drummers especially, they loved to play with me, you know. After I'd been back - East and been exposed and what not, you know. They all loved me. John Simmons, is back in town, John's back in town, you know. So naturally, I got a plenty gigs. I didn't have to look for any gigs, they could come to me, they came to me.

I'd go on them for fun, you know. Renewing old acquaintances, old lang syne, (laughter). Or this was the year that King Cole started singing. '47. He lived in a house on Avalon just across the street. Like I lived on 47th Street behind the funeral home and he lived on Avalon across the street from the funeral home. And I went over there, and offered him some grass. And it was like the most highly insult he ever received in his life. I say well what is wrong and he say, well I am singing now, John, I had to stop smoking cigarettes and everything else to protect take my voice. I say 'your voice!' I say ain't that something. I say okay. Right on. (Laughter). Okay.
